book.nourished.nourished_guide.food_safe: What happens when you eat raw food, and how your gut handles the damage.

Beyond gut health, keeping specific nutrient bars topped up builds direct **resistance** to raw food penalties — reducing how hard each event hits before it even happens. Different tiers respond to different groups:

[#](E6C65C)Mild[#]() resistance comes from [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]() and [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]().
[#](E85D75)Medium[#]() resistance comes from [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() and [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]().
[#](E85D75)Severe[#]() resistance comes from [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() and [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]().
Building Resistance
The hidden stat that makes repeated raw eating worse over time.

Your gut flora is a separate hidden stat that tracks how well your digestive system is holding up.

It starts healthy and decays when you eat raw food. Let it get low enough and it starts amplifying the penalties you take — a bad gut makes raw food even worse.
Gut Health

Every raw food event damages your gut flora by an amount based on the tier. [#](E85D75)Severe[#]() foods do the most damage, [#](E6C65C)Mild[#]() foods do the least.

Gut damage doesn't happen instantly from one bad meal — it accumulates. Eating raw occasionally is survivable. Making it a habit is not.
How It Decays

Gut flora recovers two ways. Eating **cooked** food gives an immediate boost proportional to how well-cooked it is — a fully cooked meal helps more than a barely-seared one.

It also regenerates passively over time, and that passive rate gets a **diversity bonus** the more balanced your overall diet is. A well-rounded diet across all six groups isn't just good for your bars — it heals your gut faster too.
How It Recovers
Gut Health

Cook your food whenever possible. Keep your overall diet balanced to speed up gut recovery, and pay attention to Proteins in particular — it contributes to resistance against both Medium and Severe raw food.

If your gut is already low, prioritize cooked meals until it recovers before worrying about the rest of your bars.
The Takeaway
Food Safety
What happens when you skip the campfire.

Eating raw meat and other uncooked foods [#](E85D75)isn't free[#](). Nourished tracks what you eat and penalizes you when you skip the campfire.

The penalty scales with how raw the food is — there are three tiers: **Mild**, **Medium**, and **Severe**. Foods that are fine raw (bread, apples, carrots) skip all of this entirely.
Eating Raw Food

Nourished remembers recent raw food events for a short window. If you eat the same raw item again inside that window, the system does not roll a fresh random debuff — it **extends the one you already have**, stacking its duration on top.

Back-to-back raw meals of the same item make the debuff last longer, not shorter. Switching to a cooked meal (or a different food entirely) breaks the chain.
Eating the Same Food Again

[#](E85D75)Medium[#]() penalties apply to clearly raw foods — standard raw meats like beef, pork, and chicken.

The nutrient penalty is larger and a significant portion of the nutrition is lost compared to eating the cooked version. You are also more likely to trigger gut flora damage at this tier.
Medium

[#](E6C65C)Mild[#]() penalties apply to foods that are technically edible raw but clearly not ideal — lightly processed or borderline items.

You take a small nutrient penalty and miss out on a portion of the nutrition the cooked version would have given. Not a disaster, but it adds up.
Mild

Every tier includes a **missed opportunity** multiplier. This is the fraction of nutrition the cooked version would have given that you simply don't get.

Eating raw doesn't just hurt you — it wastes the food. A raw beef gives far less Protein than a cooked one, even before the penalty kicks in.
Missed Opportunity
Raw Food

[#](E85D75)Severe[#]() penalties apply to foods that should never be eaten raw under any circumstances.

Nutrient bars take a meaningful hit, nearly all of the cooked nutrition is denied, and your gut flora takes the hardest damage. Just cook it.
Severe
book.nourished.nourished_guide.getting_s: A detailed breakdown of every food group.
The full diet screen shows detailed breakdowns of every food group and your recent eating history.

Each food group shows a **fill bar** representing your current level. Bars drain over time through nutrient decay.

Hover over a bar to see the exact value, your active bonus or penalty, and which foods you have recently eaten in that group.

When all of the food groups are above their threshold, you gain the [#](F5A623)**Balance Bonus**[#](), a persistent buff that improves health, speed, or other stats depending on your configuration.

Keeping the bonus active should be your primary goal.
Bonuses and penalties tied to each food group.

Letting any group fall to zero applies a [#](E85D75)**penalty**[#]() for that group. Penalties stack: neglecting multiple groups at once causes increasingly severe debuffs.

Recovery is straightforward: eat foods from the depleted group and the penalty fades as the bar refills.

Each food group has its own bonus active when healthy:

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#](): [#](FFB84D) increased regeneration speed.[#]()

[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#](): [#](8FE388) improved hunger saturation.[#]()

[#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#](): [#](F0808F) increased max health.[#]()

[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#](): [#](F2D77C) faster experience gain.[#]()

[#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#](): [#](8CCCF0) increased armor toughness.[#]()

Each food group has its own penalty when depleted:

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#](): [#](D98200) reduced max health.[#]()

[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#](): [#](4F9E4F) reduced movement speed.[#]()

[#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#](): [#](C43D52) reduced attack damage.[#]()

[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#](): [#](B89F32) reduced hunger restoration.[#]()

[#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#](): [#](4D91BA) reduced knockback resistance.[#]()

Effects from multiple groups stack. Having all bonuses active simultaneously gives a compound advantage across health, damage, speed, regen, XP, and armor.

Conversely, multiple penalties at once — especially [#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#]() (health) + [#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#]() (damage) + [#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#]() (knockback) — can make combat very dangerous. Prioritize preventing that combination above all else.

Your currently active Nourished bonuses and penalties are shown on the left panel of the Diet Screen. Open it to see a full list of current effects and which groups are causing them.

The HUD bar overlay gives a quick at-a-glance view of bar levels in the game world without opening any screen.

Raw meats count as [#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#](), but their nutrition values are lower than their cooked equivalents. Always cook your meat when possible.

Some foods only register as their group when prepared. Check tooltips if a food isn't filling the bar you expect.
A survival guide for your first day with Nourished active.

Eating the same food repeatedly gives less nutrition each time due to diminishing returns. Rotate through different foods within each group to maximize efficiency.

See the How It Works chapter for the full details.

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#](): Berry bushes, apple-bearing trees, and melon patches.

[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#](): Carrots, potatoes, and beetroot from villages or the ground.

[#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#](): Cooked chicken, beef, or fish from nearby animals and rivers.

Sleep when all five bars are above their threshold and wake up with the [#](B88CFF)**Sleep Bonus**[#](). This is the ideal daily rhythm Nourished is designed around.

With a bit of preparation, staying balanced becomes second nature.

[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#](): Bread from village chests, or seeds to plant wheat immediately.

[#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#](): A bucket of milk from any cow covers the dairy group in a pinch.

Once you are past day one, check out the Tips & Tricks chapter for deeper strategies:

[#](F5A623)**Daily Routine**[#](): the ideal loop for keeping all bars healthy.

[#](7BC96F)**Efficient Farming**[#](): the minimum farm that covers all five groups.

[#](E85D75)**Emergency Recovery**[#](): what to do when multiple bars crash.

[#](6FB8E8)**Reading Tooltips**[#](): food tooltips and JEI tag search.

A small mixed farm is the most reliable long-term strategy. Plant [#](E6C65C)**wheat**[#](), [#](7BC96F)**carrots**[#](), [#](7BC96F)**potatoes**[#](), and [#](7BC96F)**beetroot**[#]() early.

Keep a cow pen nearby for milk and cooked beef. Even a tiny farm can cover most of your core food groups with minimal effort.

When you first spawn, all the nutrition bars start at a moderate level. You won't feel any effects immediately, but they will begin to decay.

Your priority on day one is to gather a variety of foods before the bars run dry.
Reading a food's group and nutrition value at a glance.
The tooltip shows the food's **group**, its **nutrition value**, and its **family**. Foods from the same family give diminishing returns — variety within a group matters as much as the group itself.
Hover over any food item to see which food group it belongs to and how much nutrition it provides.

Press [#](F5A623)**H**[#]() to enter [#](B88CFF)**Edit Mode**[#](). In edit mode you can drag the HUD to any position on your screen.

Press [#](F5A623)**H**[#]() again to lock it back in place. Your [#](7BC96F)**position**[#]() is saved between sessions.

The HUD can be positioned wherever it is most convenient for you while playing.

The [#](8CCCF0)**Nutrition HUD**[#]() displays your current nutrition levels at a glance.

Each bar represents one of your food groups, making it easy to see which parts of your diet need attention without opening a screen.

[#](F5A623)**The Core Idea**[#]()

There are five food groups:

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#]()
[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#]()
[#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#]()
[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#]()
[#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#]()

Maintaining each group provides [#](6FB8E8)**bonuses**[#](), while neglecting them causes [#](E85D75)**penalties**[#](). [#](F2D77C)**Balance**[#]() is everything.
What Nourished is and how it changes the way you eat.

[#](B88CFF)**Welcome to Nourished**[#]()

Nourished adds a nutrition system that encourages eating a [#](B88CFF)**varied diet**[#](). Each food group you consume contributes to your overall [#](7BC96F)**health**[#]() and [#](F5A623)**performance**[#]().

Eat well, sleep soundly, and your body will reward you.

When a food group drops [#](E85D75)**critically low**[#](), Nourished sends a [#](F5A623)**toast notification**[#]() in the top-right corner of your screen.

Toasts appear once per group when they cross the critical threshold. Pay attention to them, or your stats will suffer.
Toast warnings when a food group runs critically low.
Nourished uses [#](F5A623)**notifications**[#]() to warn you when your nutrition needs attention.

You can disable [#](B88CFF)**notifications**[#]() in the mod's config if you prefer to manage nutrition manually.

The [#](6FB8E8)**HUD mini bars**[#]() will still change color as groups reach critical levels, giving you a passive visual warning at all times.
The reward for going to bed well-nourished.

Filling [#](7BC96F)**all Five groups**[#]() to a [#](7BC96F)**healthy level**[#]() before bed gives the [#](F2D77C)**maximum bonus**[#]() — a burst of [#](E85D75)**regeneration**[#]() and a small boost to your [#](6FB8E8)**nutrient levels**[#]() on waking.

Neglecting your diet means waking up feeling no better than when you went to sleep.
A well-balanced diet makes for better rest. When you sleep, your nutrition determines the strength of your [#](B88CFF)**Sleep Bonus**[#]() when you wake.
book.nourished.nourished_guide.how_it_wo:
The [#](B88CFF)Balance Score[#]() measures how evenly spread your nutrition is across all six groups — not how full any single bar is.

It compares each bar to the average of all of them. Five groups full and one empty scores worse than all six sitting at a moderate, even level. It's shown on the left panel of the diet screen.
Balance Score
How evenly spread your nutrition is, not how full any one bar is.

The score isn't a fixed pass/fail band — it's continuous. The further any bar drifts from the average of the rest, the more the score drops, whether that bar is unusually low or unusually high.

[#](7BC96F)Even[#]() coverage across all six groups keeps the score high. [#](E85D75)Lopsided[#]() eating — maxing one or two bars while others sit empty — drags it down even if your total nutrition looks fine on paper.
Even vs. Uneven
Balance Score
A deeper look at the systems behind Nourished.

The food tooltip shows your current freshness for any item:

[#](7BC96F)Fresh[#]() — full or bonus nutrition, novelty active.
[#](E6C65C)Reduced[#]() — diminishing returns pulling the multiplier down.
[#](E85D75)Saturated[#]() — heavily repeated, near the floor.

Check this before eating if you're trying to efficiently top up a specific bar.
Checking Your Status
Why the fifth apple of the day barely moves the bar.

Eating the same food repeatedly gives [#](E85D75)less nutrition each time[#](). The first apple of the day fills your Fruits bar noticeably. The fifth apple barely moves it.

This system exists to reward variety over repetition.
Diminishing Returns

Diminishing returns aren't tied to sleeping or the in-game day — they fade continuously based on real time elapsed since you last ate that food.

Give something a break for a while and its multiplier recovers on its own. There's no need to wait for morning; just eat something else in the meantime.
How It Fades
Diminishing Returns

Eating something you haven't touched in a while gives a [#](7BC96F)novelty bonus[#]() that pushes the multiplier above 1.0 — genuinely diverse eating gives more nutrition than the safe, familiar choice.

The tooltip shows [#](7BC96F)Fresh[#]() when the novelty bonus is active on a food.
The Novelty Bonus

Nourished tracks how much you've recently leaned on a food at three levels simultaneously: the **specific item**, its **family**, and its **food group**.

These aren't three separate penalties stacked on top of each other — they blend into one multiplier. Early on, the item-specific level dominates. The more you've recently eaten broadly from that family or group, the more those broader levels start pulling your multiplier down too.
Three Levels at Once
The middle layer between a single food and its whole group.

Within each food group, foods are organized into **families**. All apple-type foods, for example, share the Apple family.

Family is the middle of the three levels Diminishing Returns tracks — between the specific item and the whole food group. Lean on one family for a while and it starts dragging down everything in that family, not just the one item.
Food Families
Food Families

You can check a food's family in its tooltip. Ideally you want to rotate across **multiple families** within each group, not just multiple foods.

Eating an apple, then a golden apple, then an enchanted golden apple is still all Apple family — real variety means switching to melons or berries instead.
Why It Matters

Your **Balance Score** doesn't multiply nutrition directly — instead, a well-balanced diet speeds up passive Gut Health recovery, and Gut Health itself amplifies every raw-food penalty you take when it's low. See the previous entry and the Food Safety chapter for both.
Balance and Gut Health
How every bonus and penalty in this chapter fits together.
Multiplier System

None of these systems need to be memorized in detail. The practical takeaway is consistent across all of them: cook your food, rotate what you eat across items and families, and spread your meals across groups instead of running one at a time.

Do that, and most of this chapter simply never comes up.
Putting It Together

Everything in this chapter feeds into one question: how much nutrition does this specific meal actually give you? Two things can push that number up:

[#](7BC96F)Cooking:[#]() eating something cooked avoids the raw food penalty entirely — see the Food Safety chapter.
[#](7BC96F)Novelty:[#]() eating a food you haven't touched in a while gives a one-time boost on top of its normal value.
The Bonuses

And several things can push it down:

[#](E85D75)Diminishing Returns:[#]() repeating the same item, family, or group recently reduces its multiplier.
[#](E85D75)Streak:[#]() eating the exact same item again soon makes that drop steeper.
[#](E85D75)Nutritional Debt:[#]() overeating one group past a threshold drains whichever group you've neglected most.
The Penalties
How It Works

The fix is the same as everything else in this chapter: rotate. Spreading your meals across groups instead of running one group at a time keeps your eat-count on any single group below the threshold, so debt never triggers in the first place.

A high Balance Score and staying out of Nutritional Debt go hand in hand — both reward the same even, varied diet.
Avoiding It
The cost of leaning on one food group for too long.
Nutritional Debt

[#](E85D75)Nutritional Debt[#]() isn't about letting a bar sit empty — it's the cost of eating too narrowly. Lean hard on one food group over and over, past a configurable threshold, and the system starts looking for payback.
Nutritional Debt

Once that threshold is crossed, Nourished finds whichever group you've been [#](6FB8E8)neglecting[#]() the most — your lowest bar, excluding the one you're currently overeating — and drains it a little.

In other words: bingeing on Proteins doesn't just fail to help your other bars, it can actively cost you whichever one you've been ignoring.
Who Pays for It

Eating any **different food** breaks the streak immediately. You don't need to switch groups — just switch items.

The streak counter shows in the food tooltip when it's active, so you always know before you take the hit.
Breaking the Streak
Why the third bread in a row hits harder than the first.
Streak Penalty

Eating the same food back-to-back applies a [#](E85D75)Streak Penalty[#](). Three meals of plain bread in a row? The third gives noticeably less grain nutrition than the first.

A streak isn't a separate system bolted onto Diminishing Returns — it's what makes that item's diminishing-returns count climb faster than normal. Eating it again soon after adds a bigger hit to the same counter instead of a normal-sized one.
Streak Penalty
book.nourished.nourished_guide.name: Nourished Guide
book.nourished.nourished_guide.server_ow:
Nourished exposes every bonus and penalty as a status effect entry in a config file. Server owners can change which potion effect is applied, its amplifier and duration, and the nutrient threshold that triggers it — no restart required.

The config lives at [#](B88CFF)config/nourished/effects.json[#]().
Configuring Effects
Tuning the potion effects tied to each nutrient bar.

To turn off a specific bonus or penalty, set its [#](6FB8E8)enabled[#]() field to [#](6FB8E8)false[#](). The nutrient bar keeps tracking as normal — the entry is simply skipped when deciding which effects to apply.

This is useful for lighter server experiences or modpacks with their own progression systems. Built-in effects are only regenerated into the file if it is missing or invalid, so a disabled entry stays disabled.
Disabling Effects

Each entry in the array is one effect tied to one nutrient:

[#](6FB8E8)effect[#]() — the status effect id to apply, e.g. [#](6FB8E8)minecraft:weakness[#]().
[#](6FB8E8)nutrient[#]() — the nutrient key this entry watches, or [#](6FB8E8)all[#]().
[#](6FB8E8)trigger[#]() — [#](6FB8E8)below[#](), [#](6FB8E8)above[#](), or [#](6FB8E8)all_above[#](): when the effect fires relative to [#](6FB8E8)threshold[#]().
[#](6FB8E8)amplifier[#]() / [#](6FB8E8)duration_ticks[#]() — potion strength and how long it lasts.
[#](6FB8E8)enabled[#]() — set [#](6FB8E8)false[#]() to disable the entry without deleting it.
Effect Entry Fields
Configuring Effects

After editing [#](B88CFF)effects.json[#](), run [#](6FB8E8)/nourished reload[#]() to pick up the change without restarting the server.

Effects registered by other mods through the API or KubeJS are merged into this same file at runtime, so it always reflects everything currently active.
Reloading Changes
Configuration options and per-item overrides for server administrators.
Correcting or reassigning how a specific item is classified.

Nourished supports per-item [#](B88CFF)value overrides[#]() for nutrients and calories. This lets server owners and modpack makers correct or reassign how any specific item is classified without touching the mod itself.

Overrides live at [#](B88CFF)config/nourished/food_overrides.json[#]().
Food Value Overrides

Run [#](7BC96F)/marieslib dump nourished_nutrients[#]() (or the "Export All Foods" button in the Scanner tab of the config screen) to write a reference folder — one file per nutrient, listing every item Nourished currently resolves into that category with its live values.

These export files are read-only reference; editing them does nothing by itself.
Getting Starting Values

An override entry has [#](6FB8E8)item[#](), [#](6FB8E8)nutrients[#](), [#](6FB8E8)calories[#](), and [#](6FB8E8)enabled[#]() fields. It is merged over normal classification, not a full replacement:

Any nutrient key you list wins outright — including a value of [#](6FB8E8)0[#](), which zeroes that nutrient out entirely.
Any key you omit still falls back to whatever Nourished would normally classify for that item.
[#](6FB8E8)calories[#]() is always a full override when present.
How Overrides Merge
Food Value Overrides
After editing [#](B88CFF)food_overrides.json[#](), run [#](6FB8E8)/nourished reload[#]() to pick up the change without restarting the server.
Reloading Changes
Writing an Override
Server Owners
book.nourished.nourished_guide.tips_and_:
You do not need to eat from all five groups at every meal. Instead, eat 2–3 groups per sitting and rotate which groups you cover each time.

Example rotation:
**Morning:** [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]() + [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]()
**Midday:** [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]() + [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]()
**Evening:** [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]()

This keeps all bars healthy without ever feeling like a chore.
Batch Eating

Before entering a dungeon, raid, or boss fight, check that these two groups are above their good threshold:

[#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() — bonus max health helps survive burst damage.
[#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]() — bonus armor toughness reduces effective incoming damage.

If either is low, eat a cooked steak and bucket a cow before you go in. The difference in survivability is significant.
Before a Fight

Planning to enchant gear or grind a mob farm? Make sure your [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]() group is well above the bonus threshold before you start.

The Grains bonus — faster experience gain — passively increases all XP earned while active. A pumpkin pie and a loaf of bread before your session can meaningfully speed up an enchanting or leveling run.
Before an XP Session
A simple daily rhythm that keeps every bar healthy.

Glance at the HUD bar overlay regularly — not just when you feel effects. Bars drop slowly and you want to catch them before they hit the critical threshold, not after.

If a bar is in the [#](E85D75)red range[#](), address it immediately. If it is in the [#](E6C65C)yellow range[#](), eat something from that group before your next sleep.
The HUD is Your Friend

Nourished is designed around a simple daily rhythm. Follow this loop and you will rarely suffer a penalty:

**Morning:** eat one food from any low group before leaving base.
**During the day:** eat normally for hunger; rotate food types.
**Evening:** top up any bars below 50% before sleeping.
**Sleep:** with all bars healthy to earn the Sleep Bonus.
The Ideal Daily Loop
Daily Routine
Practical strategies for staying balanced, recovering quickly, and getting the most out of Nourished.

If you can only keep one or two animal pens early on, choose:

**Cows** — cover both Dairy (milk) and Proteins (cooked beef). The single most efficient animal for Nourished.
**Bees** — passive honey supply with zero daily effort once hives are set up. Useful for recipes even without a separate sweets group.

Chickens are lower priority since their protein value is lower, but they breed quickly and are easy to maintain.
Animal Priority

A few simple automations make Nourished almost invisible:

**Auto-wheat harvester** — keeps bread in constant supply.
**Dispenser + water harvester** — hands-off carrot and potato farming.
**Auto honey collector** — dispensers with bottles harvest hives automatically when full.
**Auto fish farm** — provides passive protein with no mobs required.
Automation Ideas
A small, well-planned farm covers every food group.

If you can only tend a few crops, prioritize these:

**Wheat** — most versatile; makes bread, cake, and cookies.
**Pumpkin** — makes pumpkin pie (high-value Grains).
**Melon** — the easiest renewable Fruit at scale.
**Carrots** — fast-growing, no replanting needed, renewable golden carrots.
High-Value Crops

You do not need a mega-farm to stay healthy. A surprisingly small setup covers all five groups:

**Wheat patch** — covers [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]() via bread.
**Carrot + potato rows** — covers [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]().
**Melon or berry patch** — covers [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]().
**Cow pen (2+)** — covers [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]().
**Chicken or pig pen** — covers [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]().
The Minimal Farm
Efficient Farming

Keep a dedicated **nutrition chest** near your base — a small chest stocked with one stack each of your six key foods.

Refill it during farm harvests and draw from it when a bar is low. This prevents emergency scrambles and means you always have something from each group on hand when you need it.
Storing Supplies
How to recover quickly when multiple bars hit critical.
Emergency Recovery

If a bar has been at zero for a sustained period, you may be in [#](E85D75)Nutritional Debt[#]() — a stronger debuff state. Refilling the bar does not immediately clear debt.

To recover: keep the group above zero consistently. Do not let it drop back to empty while recovering. Eat from that group multiple times over the next in-game day to work off the debt.
Nutritional Debt

Keep these high-nutrition emergency foods in your inventory for quick recovery:

**Cooked Beef** — fastest [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() top-up per item.
**Golden Carrot** — fast [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]() recovery.
**Apple** — widely available, decent [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]() nutrition.
**Milk Bucket** — instant [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]() coverage and also removes debuffs.
Quick Fix Foods

Sleep is the most powerful recovery tool in Nourished. Even if not all bars are above the bonus threshold, sleeping with all bars above **zero** prevents debt accumulation and gives a partial recovery.

If you are in a rough state, prioritize getting every bar above the critical line, then sleep. The next morning you will be in a much better position to top up properly.
Sleep to Recover

**Milk Bucket** not only fills the Dairy bar — it also removes all active status effects including nutrition penalties.

If you are stacking multiple penalties at once, drinking a milk bucket gives you a clean slate and buys time to properly address the underlying bar levels. Keep at least one in your hotbar when venturing far from home.
The Milk Trick

If multiple bars hit critical at once — maybe after a long trip far from base — do not panic. Address groups one at a time, starting with the penalty that hurts most in your current situation.

[#](E85D75)In combat or exploring:[#]() fix Proteins (attack) and Dairy (knockback) first.
[#](7BC96F)Back at base:[#]() fix Fruits (health regen) and Vegetables (saturation) for recovery.
When Things Go Wrong
Staying nourished on the road and with a crew.

For long dungeon or nether runs where you cannot eat freely between fights, prioritize **pre-loading** your bars before entering:

— All six groups above 60%
— [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() and [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]() at or above bonus threshold
— Milk bucket in hotbar for emergency debuff clear

Bars decay slowly enough that a two-hour session rarely causes a problem if you start fully topped up.
Long Dungeon Runs
Multiplayer & Adventure

In multiplayer, a shared farm benefits everyone. Consider assigning different players to maintain different groups:

**Farmer** — wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot.
**Rancher** — cows, pigs, chickens, bees.
**Forager** — collects wild fruits, mushrooms, fishing.

A well-organized community farm makes Nourished invisible for the whole server.
Shared Farms

Village trading is an underrated nutrition tool. Farmer villagers often sell:

**Bread** — cheap Grains in bulk.
**Apple** — easy early Fruits.
**Cooked Chicken** — decent Proteins trade.
**Pumpkin Pie** — excellent value Grains.

Early-game trading can cover multiple nutrition groups before your own farm is established.
Trading for Nutrition

When leaving base for extended exploration, pack food from all six groups — not just your usual hunger food. A nutrition emergency two thousand blocks from home is much worse than one in your base.

A good travel kit: cooked beef, carrot, apple, bread, honey bottle, and a milk bucket. That covers all six groups in six inventory slots.
Traveling Far from Base
Tips & Tricks
Reading a food's group, nutrition, and freshness at a glance.

Hover over any food item to see Nourished tooltip information below the item name:

**Food Group** — which bar this food fills.
**Nutrition Value** — how much it fills the bar under ideal conditions.
**Food Family** — which family it belongs to for diminishing returns.
**Freshness** — whether this food currently gives full, reduced, or bonus nutrition.
Food Tooltips

The [#](7BC96F)freshness indicator[#]() tells you how much nutrition you will actually receive:

[#](7BC96F)Fresh[#]() — first time eating this food today; full or bonus nutrition.
[#](E6C65C)Reduced[#]() — diminishing returns active; lower nutrition than base.
[#](E85D75)Saturated[#]() — heavily repeated; minimal nutrition gain.

If a food shows Saturated, switch to a different family within that group for better returns.
Freshness Indicator

If you have JEI installed, you can filter the entire item list by food group. Type any of these into the JEI search bar:

**nourished:nutrients/fruits**
**nourished:nutrients/vegetables**
**nourished:nutrients/proteins**
**nourished:nutrients/grains**
**nourished:nutrients/dairy**
JEI Tag Search

This is the fastest way to answer the question **"what can I eat right now?"** when a bar is low.

JEI will show every item on the server assigned to that group — including modded foods — so you can see at a glance what you have in your inventory or nearby chests that qualifies.
JEI Tag Search (cont.)
Reading Tooltips

When the streak penalty is active, the tooltip shows a [#](E85D75)streak counter[#](). This appears after eating the same food consecutively without switching.

If you see this, eat one different food before continuing with your usual diet. Even a single item from a different food family resets the streak and restores full multipliers.
Streak Warning

If a food item shows **Unclassified** or no Nourished tooltip at all, it has not been assigned to a food group on this server.

For modded foods this is usually resolved by the server's datapack configuration. If you believe a food should belong to a specific group, contact your server admin or check the Nourished datapack documentation in the **Server Owners** chapter.
